expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: Union with four status-keyed variants: trialing, active, past_due, canceled

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each union member carries only its own fields; trialing has trialEndDate, active has renewalDate, canceled has cancellation

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function provided; used in describeStatus switch with default: return assertNever(sub)

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId and CustomerId branded using Brand<T, B> pattern with unique symbol

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: isLegalTransition provided only as a TODO stub with example comment; not implemented

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Misuse enumeration lists 5 items including field/status mismatches, silent undefined reads, reason/voluntary drift, new status failing build; Rungs section names Control mechanisms

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union; explicitly contrasts with optional bags throughout
